name: Catuquinaru-Bach
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Unclassifiable extinct languoid (Brazil, NOCODE); Glottolog lists no descriptive references

sources.note: No references listed at all; AES extinct; Unclassifiable.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center. p.115 (entry 'Catuquinarú'), p.116 (comparative table, Tupi stock Central group II).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. 'Catuquinarú - language of a tupinized Katukina tribe, spoken on the Embira River, Amazonas. [Bach in Church 1898, p. 64.]' plus five re-spelled items in a comparative table (taka-sü, sana, punü, uhehü..). Classification only.

sources.citation: Church, George Earl. 1898. Notes on the visit of Dr. Bach to the Catuquinarú Indians of Amazonas. The Geographical Journal 12(1): 63-67. doi:10.2307/1774499 (archive.org item sim_geographical-journal_1898-07_12_1, pdf pp. 71-75)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. p.64 gives only 'Their language is very similar to that of the Miranhas of Amazonas, and has a few words of the Therena of Western Matto Grosso. The following vocabulary will give an idea of it' followed by 4 phrases and c. 30 words. Forms carry acute accents, mostly on the final vowel (Tacasú, Anahé, Cesá, Agahó, Yayoruá, Yanó, Getemaupú, Pihú, Ocausú, Carynosú, Uhÿnasú, Comatÿnú; also téna, hé-pÿ, Tinoâ) with no stated convention; no remark on pronunciation or accent anywhere in the article (pp. 63-67 read in full).
